dedupe_keys.name: acjv coastal marsh project database atlantic coast salt marsh restoration projects

description: The ACJV Coastal Marsh Project Database catalogues salt marsh restoration, management and enhancement projects along the US Atlantic coast, such as ditch remediation and runnelling to reverse marsh subsidence. The Atlantic Coast Joint Venture, a partnership of agencies and conservation groups, keeps it as part of its coastal marsh conservation framework built around three flagship species (Saltmarsh Sparrow, Black Rail and American Black Duck), and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service publishes it on its open data site. The layer holds 345 project points with names, states and descriptions of techniques, was first published in September 2024 and was last edited in September 2026. Coverage is the Atlantic coast from Maine southward. Format and access: ArcGIS Hub downloads and a feature service. Licence: the USFWS data disclaimer, with no licence named; free. Caveats: entries are contributed by partners and vary in detail, and project outcomes are not measured in the layer. Salt marshes buffer storm surge and erosion, so the inventory helps map nature-based coastal defences for climate adaptation studies. Related catalogue records are the NOAA C-CAP regional land cover and the US National Wetlands Inventory.
